phases.name: fresh-boot
phases.description: First boot of the baseline: no logon, and no password-bearing logon observed since boot; network and file probes run before any credential control. Complete event delivery is not established, so the absence is observed, not proven.

phases.name: lifecycle
phases.description: Lifecycle, recovery and revocation cases, still with no password-bearing logon observed since each boot.

phases.name: password-and-wts
phases.description: Password-bearing controls and genuine interactive sessions.

phases.name: owner-runners
phases.description: Native test-owner runners with the broker stopped and profiles unloaded.

G1.title: Interactive WTS user-manager crash loop
G1.expect: Each attempt is a successful native creation followed by a short-lived exit; the delay grows 1/2/4/8/16/32/60 and stays capped for at least five retries over ten minutes, with no renewed short delays; the peer stays healthy.

G2.title: Headless S4U user-manager crash loop
G2.expect: As G1 through the linger path with no logon; the reversible failure is then repaired and the manager recovers on its own.

G3.title: Confirmed stable runtime resets the recovery delay
G3.expect: After the delay has grown, a manager observed alive for over two minutes is killed; its replacements grow from 1 again instead of keeping the capped delay.

G4.title: Waiting recovery cancellation and broker crash recovery
G4.expect: A waiting capped recovery is cancelled by the applied policy or stop, every owned process and profile drains, and nothing is relaunched for at least two capped periods; the orderly broker stop is followed by a restart with the grant revoked, which restores nothing. The broker crash is H09's event.

G5.title: Unlimited unit recovery under a healthy headless manager
G5.expect: A short-lived nonzero-exit unit with StartLimitBurst=0 and a short capped exponential delay keeps retrying for ten minutes and more than twenty failures, more than five accepted starts in one real ten-second window, unlimited status and a confirmed stop. The finite control stops at its start limit.

G6.title: #253/#255 startup and daemon-log regressions
G6.expect: Named regressions run without skipping in their real token lanes; startup, diagnostics persistence, rotation, protection, peer denial and legacy repair hold on this artifact.

B01.title: Capped user-host retries for short-lived managers

B03.title: Grant revocation cancels a waiting retry

B04.title: Broker stop cancels a waiting retry; restart with a revoked grant restores nothing

H01.title: Cold boot, first-use profile
H01.expect: With no prior profile, registration or logon, the boot creates and loads A's profile and starts a genuine session-zero S4U manager and the enabled workload without controller intervention.

H02.title: Cold boot, existing profile
H02.expect: The same boot starts B's genuine S4U manager and workload on its existing, previously unloaded profile; both accounts progress concurrently.

H03.title: No implicit grant
H03.expect: With linger removed and the enabled units left in place, a reboot starts no headless manager or workload; explicit re-enable recovers.

H04.title: Same-account session leaves the headless manager
H04.expect: A genuine WTS logon and logoff of the account leave the headless manager, workload, AuthenticationId, session zero and headless-s4u mode unchanged.

H05.title: Revocation
H05.expect: Disabling linger with no session drains every owned process and the profile; nothing returns for the observation window or after a reboot; the peer is preserved.

H06.title: Independent permissions
H06.expect: Linger stays effective when only interactive admission changes; disabling linger while a session remains admitted keeps the session-backed manager until the final logoff drains it.

H07.title: Unit crash
H07.expect: The old unit tree exits before the new invocation is accepted; the user manager and the peer are unaffected.

H08.title: User-manager crash
H08.expect: The old owned tree exits before a new genuine S4U manager and the enabled work recover without a controller start.

H09.title: Broker crash
H09.expect: SCM recovery under the recorded policy restarts the broker and both accounts' enabled workloads; the old trees exit first; no controller restart.

H11.title: Unlimited unit retries
H11.expect: See G5: an unlimited budget is shown only by more than five accepted starts in one ten-second window, against a finite control.

H12.title: Startup and rotation
H12.expect: With a padded stopped log, the product rotates it on reopen, persists fresh protected diagnostics and stays healthy; the padding is a declared intervention.

H13.title: Own roots and state
H13.expect: The workload reads its unit fixture, writes flushed state, resolves HKCU and known folders; the peer's root is denied.

H14.title: Missing and denied roots
H14.expect: An absent path fails as not found and a SYSTEM-owned path as access denied, visibly; restoring the good path recovers.

H15.title: Authorized SYSTEM qualification pipe
H15.expect: The in-unit workload and an outside-unit process of the same account are accepted on account and held incarnation; the wrong account, an exited caller and a stale claim are denied.

H16.title: Pipe denial
H16.expect: A SYSTEM-only pipe, the peer's user pipe and the production control and maintenance pipes deny the account with ACCESS_DENIED; SYSTEM stays healthy.

H17.title: Transport
H17.expect: Loopback and isolated-peer nonce round trips from the workload token; qualifies this route only.

H18.title: Authenticated SMB
H18.expect: Bare S4U UNC access with no supplied credentials is characterized against a reachable share and a password-bearing control; no guest or machine access is credited.

H19.title: EFS
H19.expect: A plaintext read of B's encrypted fixture under bare S4U is characterized against the volume capability, a plain sibling and a same-account password decryption.

H20.title: Held native launch (#229 headless tests)
H20.expect: Accepted decisions and the held suspended stage with real S4U, profile and desktop; retained ownership on deadline; release and retry drain; zero skips. Five fresh SYSTEM runners, three cases each.

H21.title: Native inherited handles
H21.expect: The headless security test excludes sentinel inheritance with exact file-object identity and real pipe authorization; the sensitivity control, which runs with the runner's own SYSTEM token, proves the probe detects deliberate inheritance.

H22.title: Final cleanup
H22.expect: Before the snapshot revert, no owned daemon, helper, workload or client process, fixture pipe or grant remains; every account's profile hive is unloaded and its qualification state removed; the fixture's tasks, firewall rules and Default-template files are absent, as the sealed baseline requires; and the service configuration, the data root, linger and admission-policy security and content, and the audit policy equal the baseline receipt. Peer and network-route restoration is the lab controller's own record.
